questions.q: What is David crying out to Yahweh?
questions.a: He is crying out for Yahweh to come to help him and to listen to him when he calls.

questions.q: What does David want his prayer and lifted hands to be like for Yahweh?
questions.a: David wants Yahweh to accept his prayer as though it were an offering of incense to Yahweh and his hands lifted in prayer as an evening sacrifice.

questions.q: What does David ask Yahweh to guard?
questions.a: He asks Yahweh guard him against saying things that are bad or wrong.

questions.q: What does David want Yahweh to prevent him from doing?
questions.a: He asks Yahweh to prevent him from wanting to do evil things, joining wicked men in their deeds, and eating their delicacies.

questions.q: What does David say it means if a righteous man corrects him?
questions.a: He says if it is a righteous person who strikes him, he is acting faithfully and kindly toward David to correct him.

questions.q: What does David say it will be like if a righteous man corrects him?
questions.a: He says it will be as if they have honored him by anointing his head with oil, which he will not refuse.

questions.q: What does David always pray against wickedness?
questions.a: He always prays that Yahweh will punish the wicked because of the wicked deeds that they do.

questions.q: What will happen to the wicked people’s judges?
questions.a: Their judges will be thrown down from a cliff, and the wicked will hear that David’s words are right and good.

questions.q: What do the wicked say will happen to their bones?
questions.a: They say their bones will be scattered on the way to the place where dead people are, just as the earth is scattered when the ground is broken up.
David is relying on Yahweh to protect his life.

questions.q: From what does David want Yahweh to protect him?
questions.a: David wants Yahweh to protect him from the snares of people who do evil things by trying to trap and trick him.

questions.q: What does David want to happen to the wicked?
questions.a: David wants the wicked to fall into their own traps that they set to catch him while he escapes.

commentary.text: David prays for God's acceptance and assistance.
That God would appear for his rescue.

Verses 1–4 Make haste unto me. Those that know how to value God's gracious presence, will be the more fervent in their prayers. When presented through the sacrifice and intercession of the Saviour, they will be as acceptable to God as the daily sacrifices and burnings of incense were of old. Prayer is a spiritual sacrifice, it is the offering up the soul and its best affections. Good men know the evil of tongue sins. When enemies are provoking, we are in danger of speaking unadvisedly. While we live in an evil world, and have such evil hearts, we have need to pray that we may neither be drawn nor driven to do any thing sinful. Sinners pretend to find dainties in sin; but those that consider how soon sin will turn into bitterness, will dread such dainties, and pray to God to take them out of their sight, and by his grace to turn their hearts against them. Good men pray against the sweets of sin.

We should be ready to welcome the rebuke of our heavenly Father, and also the reproof of our brethren. It shall not break my head, if it may but help to break my heart: we must show that we take it kindly. Those who slighted the word of God before, will be glad of it when in affliction, for that opens the ear to instruction. When the world is bitter, the word is sweet. Let us lift our prayer unto God. Let us entreat him to rescue us from the snares of Satan, and of all the workers of iniquity. In language like this psalm, O Lord, would we entreat that our poor prayers should set forth our only hope, our only dependence on thee. Grant us thy grace, that we may be prepared for this employment, being clothed with thy righteousness, and having all the gifts of thy Spirit planted in our hearts.
